title: Wishing About Someone Else: szeretném, ha + te/ő

sections.title: The subject inside the wish can be anyone
sections.content: So far every ha-clause after szeretném has had its own subject — a tervem, az álmom, időm. Wishing about a specific person works the same way, just with the conditional matching that person instead: te becomes eljönnél/megértenéd, ő becomes eljönne/megértené. szeretném itself never changes — you are always the one wishing, no matter who or what you're wishing about.

sections.title: Matching the conditional to the wished-about person
rows: you understand it → (that) you would understand it
it succeeds for him/her → (that) it would succeed for him/her

items.spanish: Szeretném, ha eljönnél velem erre az útra.
items.english: I wish you would come with me on this trip.

items.spanish: Szeretném, ha megértenéd, miért fontos ez nekem.
items.english: I wish you would understand why this is important to me.

items.spanish: Szeretném, ha sikerülne neki elérnie a célját.
items.english: I wish he/she would succeed in reaching his/her goal.

sections.content: Don't confuse eljönnél ("you would come") with eljönne ("he/she would come") — the -nél ending marks te, the plain -ne marks ő. Since Hungarian usually drops subject pronouns, this ending is often the only clue who the wish is actually about.
